kept.excerpt: In the June primary, N’Kiyla Jasmine Thomas led the five-way Democratic primary with 45% of the vote, and Jim Priest followed with nearly 24%. State law requires a runoff when no candidate in a primary earns more than half the vote. Neither Thomas nor Priest has held elected office before. Priest, a lawyer and nonprofit executive, ran in 2010 to serve as state Attorney General and lost to Republican Scott Pruitt.
kept.relevance: This contemporaneous profile establishes Thomas’s substantial first-round lead and confirms that the nomination still required a runoff.

kept.excerpt: In an Aug. 25 runoff election, Oklahoma voters will choose the Democratic nominee to replace Markwayne Mullin in the U.S. Senate after his March appointment to lead the Department of Homeland Security. The winner of the runoff will face Republican Kevin Hern in the general election in November. Hern has served as the Congressman for Oklahoma’s first district since 2018 and swept the Republican primary in June.
kept.relevance: The opponent’s interview provides a dated preview of the remaining nomination contest and distinguishes it from the November general election.

kept.excerpt: Democrat: The race remains undecided, as N’Kiyla Jasmine Thomas (who received 45.2% of the vote) and Jim Priest (23.9%) head to a runoff. Thomas’ platform supports K-12 funding, universal healthcare and government transparency. Priest is an ordained minister and employment-law attorney in favor of keeping rural hospitals open and lowering the cost of living.
kept.relevance: Independent reporting supplies more precise first-round percentages and identifies the two candidates’ campaign platforms before the cutoff.

kept.excerpt: State Election Board Secretary Paul Ziriax announced today that no political party filed a notice to allow Independents to vote in its primaries and runoff primaries during the 2026-2027 election years. Since no political party provided a notification to the State Election Board Secretary by the statutory deadline, all primaries will remain closed for the 2026-2027 election years. Voters who would like to change their party affiliation should do so before April 1, 2026. State law prohibits party affiliation changes April 1 through August 31 of even-numbered years.
kept.relevance: This official announcement defines the eligible runoff electorate and excludes independent or Republican crossover participation in the Democratic nomination vote.

kept.excerpt: The calendar lists August 25, 2026, for Runoff Primary Elections, with Election Day hours of 7 A.M. to 7 P.M. It lists July 31 as the voter-registration deadline and August 10 as the absentee-ballot request deadline. Early voting is scheduled for August 20–21 from 8 A.M. to 6 P.M. and August 22 from 8 A.M. to 2 P.M.
kept.relevance: The dated official calendar fixes the nomination timetable and shows that the scheduled runoff was still ahead of the experiment date.
